checks.what: Prussia gain of 1830 (counterpart nobody) over Cliopatria's 'German Confederation' 1840 row, which is Prussia's provinces (1,228 cells, 5.9-22.7 E; the dossier's own 1815 and 1834 keyframes use this row). The page gives 'a province of the Kingdom of Prussia from 1829 to 1878', the cabinet order of 3 December 1829, and West Prussia with its capital at Danzig after 1815. In the trial it moves exactly the 145 cells the draft's 1834 snap filled, the same cell set: Pomeranian 61, Kuyavian-Pomeranian 50, Warmian-Masurian 7, Greater Poland 6, West Pomeranian 6, a few elsewhere. Prussia now has 1,206 cells in 1833 and 1,209 from 1834, as before. Side effect: the 1834 keyframe no longer snaps. And 6 border cells stay with their holders instead of passing to Prussia: Birkenfeld (Oldenburg) 2, Netherlands 1, Belgium 1, Saxe-Coburg 1, Neuchatel 1. The Birkenfeld change is an improvement. The rest are negligible. The window agent was wrong that the gain hands Eifel/Saar cells to Prussia in 1830-1833: it does not.

Spanish loss of 1830 to republic-of-peru, region Peru. Only Spanish-held cells move: the 37 leftovers (16 are Lake Titicaca's own cells, the rest the Titicaca shore and the Ucayali border, 16.4-2.8 S). The page gives 'The Spanish coastal fortifications in Veracruz, Callao and Chiloé were the footholds that resisted until 1825–1826' and 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule'. The Spanish specks are gone 1830-1839. Remaining defect, not caused by this entry: republic-of-peru_1834 does not hold these 37 cells, so its 1834 snap turns them grey for 1834-1835. The Confederation takes 36 in 1836, and in 1839 its ledger/10 leaves 21-22 Titicaca cells grey. A hole is better than the Spanish speck.

Spanish loss of 1830 to bolivia of the 2 leftover Beni cells (12.6-10.8 S, 65.5-64.1 W). The page gives 'the royalist troops of Upper Peru under the command of Olañeta surrendered after he died in Tumusla on 2 April 1825'. The cells stay Bolivian through 1839 in the trial.

Spanish loss of 1830 of the 8 Rio Negro mouth cells (41.0-40.7 S, 63.2-62.7 W, Carmen de Patagones). The removal of Spain is right (wars page, as in events/1). But counterpart 'nobody' left them grey in 1830, and rio-de-la-plata, whose 1830 shape holds them, passes them to the Argentine Confederation in 1831. The Carmen de Patagones page I opened: 'The town was founded in 1779 by Francisco de Viedma'; 'after the May Revolution of 1810, it became a prison for royalists'; 'The Brazilian troops attempted to take Carmen de Patagones, but they were repelled by armed residents on 7 March 1827'. It was not Spanish and not empty. After the fix the trial moves them spanish-empire -> rio-de-la-plata in 1830 and to the Argentine Confederation in 1831 (ledger/0). The p1840 end anchor is identical to the unfixed trial.

muhammad-ali-dynasty_1839 (1839 only): the dossier correction with Hasa cut to Hasa ∩ Emirate of Nejd 1830. That is 490 of 2,447 cells, 24.0-28.5 N, 45.5-50.7 E, and includes Hofuf and Qatif. The page gives 'Mehmet Ali had occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif' and 'in 1838 Mehmet Ali's forces commanded by Hurshid Pasha marched against Faisal and defeated him' (recall 'in April 1840'). In the trial the 1839 snap adds 689 instead of 2,632 cells, Hasa's 1,943 Empty Quarter cells stay unowned, and the Trucial States conflict (14) is gone. The 490 Hasa cells are exactly what ledger/18 took from Nejd in 1838, so 1838 and 1839 agree. Residual, not this entry's claim: the 689 cells still added are the gazetteer's Najd (Ar Riyad province) south of what Nejd held, 19.3-23.9 N. They include inhabited southern Najd (As Sulayyil/Wadi ad-Dawasir, al-Aflaj), which the page's 'Najd' covers, but also the western edge of the Rub' al-Khali at 19-21 N, 46-48 E. The agent's report that the 'Empty Quarter' is unowned is only true for its Hasa part.
